title: Boss: LogTools 1.2.0 is red
summary: A failing CI run to read and fix in the code, a test that quietly calls the real API, and an installed module that will not load. Fix each at the cause.

steps.title: Ticket TOOLS-58
body: *"LogTools 1.2.0 is blocked: the pipeline is red, one test needs the internet (the build agents have none), and on
Priya's machine `Import-Module LogTools` says no valid module file was found. Release is Friday."*
Read the evidence first (`~/ci/pester-run.log`, the test output, the import error), then fix the real cause. A test
is wrong only when it asserts the wrong behaviour; otherwise fix the code.

steps.title: Red pipeline: keeps 90 days of audit logs
prompt: Read the pipeline's output, `Get-Content ~/ci/pester-run.log`, and reproduce it:
The test is right: audit logs are kept for 90 days, and `-Days` must accept that (up to 3650, as before 1.2.0).
Fix **the module**, not the test, so the file passes.

checks.name: the test itself is unchanged
checks.fail: Change the module, not `tests/Get-OldLog.Tests.ps1` (`git diff tests/` shows what you changed; `git checkout -- tests/Get-OldLog.Tests.ps1` puts it back).

checks.name: -Days is still validated
checks.cmd: pwsh -NoProfile -c 'Import-Module ~/src/LogTools/LogTools.psd1; try { Get-OldLog -Path /tmp -Days 0; "accepted 0" } catch { "refused 0" }; try { $null = Get-OldLog -Path /tmp -Days 3650; "accepted 3650" } catch { "refused 3650" }'
checks.fail: `-Days` should accept 1 to 3650 and still refuse 0.

hints: The log says *Cannot validate argument on parameter 'Days'. The 90 argument is greater than the maximum allowed range of 30*.
Look at `Get-OldLog`'s `param()` in `~/src/LogTools/LogTools.psm1`: `git diff HEAD~1 -- LogTools.psm1` shows what 1.2.0 changed.
steps.explain: The test protected a real requirement (audit retention) from a well-meant "tightening". When a test goes red, the first question is *which one is wrong, the code or the test?*, and `git diff` of the last change usually answers it in a minute.

steps.title: The test that needs the internet
prompt: `Invoke-RestMethod`, yet the failure is a network error from the **real** `Invoke-RestMethod` (this machine, like the
Fix the **test** this time so the mock is used and the test passes, with no network.

checks.name: the mock and the assertion target the module
checks.fail: Both `Mock Invoke-RestMethod` and `Should -Invoke Invoke-RestMethod` need `-ModuleName LogTools`.

checks.name: it still checks what was sent
checks.fail: Keep the `-ParameterFilter` that checks the body says `oldFiles = 1`: that is what the test is for.

hints: `Send-LogSummary` runs inside the LogTools module; the test's `Mock` lives in the test's scope.
Add `-ModuleName LogTools` to the `Mock` line **and** to `Should -Invoke`.

`(Get-Content $f -Raw).Replace('Mock Invoke-RestMethod {', 'Mock Invoke-RestMethod -ModuleName LogTools {').Replace('Should -Invoke Invoke-RestMethod', 'Should -Invoke Invoke-RestMethod -ModuleName LogTools')`
solution: (Get-Content $f -Raw).Replace('Mock Invoke-RestMethod {', 'Mock Invoke-RestMethod -ModuleName LogTools {').Replace('Should -Invoke Invoke-RestMethod', 'Should -Invoke Invoke-RestMethod -ModuleName LogTools') | Set-Content $f -NoNewline
explain: On a developer laptop with internet, this test "passed" by posting to the real dashboard on every run, which is
worse than failing. Build agents without network caught it. A unit test that can reach the network is a bug; Pester
6 shows the recorded invocations of a mock when `Should -Invoke` fails, which makes this one easy to spot.

steps.title: No valid module file was found
prompt: A colleague copied LogTools 1.2.0 into `~/.local/share/powershell/Modules/LogTools/1.2.0/`. Try
`Import-Module LogTools` and read the error, then compare the folder name with what the manifest inside says
This **is** release 1.2.0. Fix the installed copy so `Import-Module LogTools` loads version **1.2.0**.

checks.name: Import-Module LogTools loads 1.2.0
checks.fail: `Import-Module LogTools` should load version 1.2.0 from your module folder.

checks.name: the installed manifest is valid and exports Send-LogSummary
checks.fail: The manifest in the `1.2.0` folder should say `ModuleVersion = '1.2.0'` and export `Send-LogSummary`.

hints: PowerShell only accepts a module in a version folder when the manifest's `ModuleVersion` matches the folder name. Otherwise it skips it and reports *no valid module file was found*.

`Update-ModuleManifest` refuses a manifest that does not match its folder, so edit the text: `$p = '~/.local/share/powershell/Modules/LogTools/1.2.0/LogTools.psd1'; (Get-Content $p -Raw).Replace("ModuleVersion = '1.1.0'", "ModuleVersion = '1.2.0'") | Set-Content $p -NoNewline`
explain: Hand-copying modules is how this happens. Installing from the feed (`Install-PSResource LogTools -Version 1.2.0`)
always creates a folder that matches the package's manifest, and `Get-InstalledPSResource` can then tell you exactly
